title: Run prototype and pilot production builds (EVT, DVT and PVT)
summary: Hardware is built several times before mass production. Each build has a purpose and exit criteria: first the design works, then it is right, then the factory can make it.

beginner: Learn the three builds: engineering validation (EVT), design validation (DVT) and production validation (PVT).
For each build, write down what it must prove before the next one starts.
Agree how many units each build needs, including extras for testing and marketing.
Track the issues found in each build and who is fixing them.
Do not move to the next build until the exit criteria are met.
intermediate: Plan the build schedule with time to fix issues between builds.
Agree exit criteria for each build with engineering and the manufacturer.
Shorten the build, test and fix cycle rather than squeezing the schedule.
experienced: Set build standards across products so schedules are comparable.
Decide when an extra build is cheaper than shipping a known problem.
Report build readiness to leadership with clear risks.

canDelegateTo.task: Agree exit criteria and the build schedule
Run the tests for each build

toolExamples.jira: Track issues by build, such as EVT or DVT.
toolExamples.confluence: Write the exit criteria for each build on one page.

definitionOfDone: Exit criteria written for each build
Issues tracked to closure before the next build
pitfalls: Calling a build DVT when the design is still changing
Squeezing the schedule instead of fixing faster
